subsystems.name: Anode
subsystems.role: stores lithium and sets much of the cell's capacity; a solid electrolyte allows lithium metal here instead of graphite.

subsystems.name: Solid electrolyte
subsystems.role: conducts lithium ions between the electrodes while physically blocking the dendrites that cause fires in liquid cells.
parts: sulfide or oxide ceramic (e.g. garnet-type) powder

subsystems.name: Cathode
subsystems.role: the lithium source on first charge; must be mixed with solid electrolyte rather than soaked in liquid.

subsystems.name: Cell stack and interfaces
subsystems.role: intimate contact between rigid layers, kept under pressure so ions can cross every boundary.

subsystems.name: Battery management and conversion
subsystems.role: a single cell outputs roughly 3–4 V, so electronics must regulate charging and boost to the 5 V USB output.

subsystems.name: Pack and enclosure
subsystems.role: holds the cells, spreads heat and provides the pocket-sized case and ports.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the electrolyte
buildSteps.detail: Sulfide glass-ceramic is milled from raw powders and heat-treated; oxide versions are sintered at over 1000 °C. Both are processed in dry rooms or inert gas, because sulfides react with moisture.

buildSteps.title: Form the membrane
buildSteps.detail: The electrolyte is pressed or cast into a dense sheet tens of micrometres thick — thin enough for low resistance, thick enough to stop dendrites.

buildSteps.title: Make the cathode composite
buildSteps.detail: Cathode powder is mixed with electrolyte particles and carbon, then coated onto aluminium foil and rolled flat.

buildSteps.title: Stack and densify
buildSteps.detail: Cathode, electrolyte and anode are laminated and pressed, sometimes warm-pressed or sintered, to close the microscopic gaps between layers.

buildSteps.title: Package the cells
buildSteps.detail: Cells are cut and sealed into laminated pouches or ceramic packages with welded tabs; sealing quality decides life and safety.

buildSteps.title: Form and test
buildSteps.detail: The first slow charge forms the interfaces; cells are then tested for capacity, resistance and self-discharge, and aged at elevated temperature.

buildSteps.title: Build the pack
buildSteps.detail: Cells are connected in series-parallel, bonded to a circuit board with the charge controller, boost converter and USB-C port.

buildSteps.title: Enclose and certify
buildSteps.detail: The pack goes into the shell with thermal padding and is drop-tested and safety-tested, including the UN 38.3 transport standard for lithium batteries.

prerequisites.tech: Solid electrolytes with high room-temperature ionic conductivity
prerequisites.why: sulfide ceramics can reach ionic conductivities comparable to liquid electrolytes in the lab; keeping that performance in a manufactured sheet is harder.
without a liquid to wet the surfaces, contact is poor and resistance grows, shortening life.
many promising electrolytes degrade in ordinary humid air, so existing lithium-ion factories cannot simply be reused.
sintering large, defect-free ceramic sheets cheaply is not yet a proven mass-production process.

prerequisites.tech: Stack-pressure management in a pocket device
prerequisites.why: cells need sustained mechanical pressure; doing that in a thin, drop-tested consumer product is an engineering compromise.

pathway.milestone: tiny ceramic and thin-film solid-state cells shipping in wearables and sensors
pathway.unlocks: real-world data on solid-state lifetime in small formats.

pathway.milestone: pilot production lines for larger sulfide-based cells, initially for electric vehicles
pathway.unlocks: falling cell costs and evidence that the chemistry scales beyond button size.

pathway.milestone: solid-state power banks and phones using the same cells
pathway.unlocks: thinner, faster-charging gadgets that are far less likely to catch fire.

pathway.milestone: solid-state cells become the default in premium devices
pathway.unlocks: higher energy density per kilogram and per litre across portable electronics — if ceramic manufacturing and cost targets are met.
